title: Let closed-task cleanup complete hidden or partly removed worktrees natively without asking Greg
outcome: Let closed-task cleanup complete hidden or partly removed worktrees natively without asking Greg
acceptance: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md "Cleanup deletions" (and the matching .logs/.evidence and worktree bullets) say that cleanup when all items the target served are closed proceeds without asking Greg, with the existing path, retention, live-work and unpushed-change checks kept; that when the non-forced form leaves hidden, read-only or partly removed content, the native completion `git worktree remove --force <checked path>` with a single `--force` (for a registered worktree) or `Remove-Item -LiteralPath <checked path> -Recurse -Force -Confirm:$false` (for a plain directory inside the repository) is allowed, and any remaining worktree registration is left in place and reported; and that every other failure still stops and is reported. The wording matches the text agreed for TermAl w-c969a2bea0d9.

Markdown only; both files stay identical; the focused launcher link check passes; a Codex plus Claude pair reviews it; the authority-text conditions (a) both coordinators' concurrence on the exact wording, (b) the wording sent to Greg, (c) a recorded final-diff audit, and Greg's verbatim word for the widening are recorded on the item before landing.
